sentences.text: This petition is filed by the Petitioners against Respondent No.1 to 6 under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1994 for the relief of compensation.
SCCH 5 2.

The brief facts of the case is as under; That on 09.02.2023 at about 7.00 a.m. Raj kumar @ Raja Kamara was riding scooter bearing Reg. No.KA- 50-EH-7381 on 2nd Cross, Kodigehalli, Opp. True Medical Health Partner, Thindlu Main Road, Bengaluru, at that time, a driver of School Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-50-B- 2090 came in rash and negligent manner without observing traffic rules and regulations and dashed against him, consequent to which, he fell down, sustained grievous injuries and became unconscious.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Med Star Hospital, after first aid treatment, he was referred to Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as inpatient, even after better and expert treatment, Rajkumar was succumbed to the injuries on 12.02.2023 at about 8.30 a.m., post mortem was conducted at Victoria Hospital and body was handed over to the SCCH 5 petitioners, they have performed funeral and obsequies ceremony, by spending more than Rs.3,00,000/- towards medical expenses and other charges.

3. Prior to the accident, deceased RajKumar was hale and healthy, aged about 40 years, working as Helper and Delivery man at Sri Laxmi Enterprises and Dunza, thereby earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.
Due to sudden and sad demise of the deceased, petitioners are undergoing deep mental shock, pain and suffering and they are put to great financial hardship without earning member of the family.
Petitioner No.1 and 2 are parents, petitioner No.3 and 4 are minor daughters of the deceased.
Petitioner No.3 and 4 have born to first wife of the deceased by name Ankita, who expired on 29.03.2020 and respondent No.3 is 2nd wife of the deceased.

The accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of school bus by its driver and crime No.43/2023 is registered against SCCH 5 him before the Hebbal Traffic Police for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337 and 304(A) of IPC.
Respondent No.1 is R.C.Owner and respondent No.2 is insurer of the offending vehicle, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- with interest.
4. In pursuance of service of notice, respondent No.1/owner has remained absent, hence placed exparte.
Respondent No.2 being the insurer has appeared and filed written statement and denied averments of the petition.
Further submitted that, it had issued insurance policy in respect of school bus bearing Reg. No.KA-50-B- 2090 and its liability is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
Further submitted that, driver of the said offending vehicle does not possess valid and effective driving licence and said vehicle has not permit to ply in a place of accident.
Respondent No.2 is entitled to seek SCCH 5 protection available under Sec.147 and 149 of M.V.Act.
There is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and Sec.158(6) of M.V.Act.
Further denied age, occupation and income of the deceased.
Compensation claimed by the petitioner is on higher side.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.
5. Respondent No.3/ 2nd wife of the deceased has appeared through counsel and filed written statement and submitted that, she is legally wedded wife of the deceased Rajkumar.
Further submitted that, she got married with deceased on 30.05.2021.

Further submitted that, she has lost her husband within span of 2 years of her married life and she has lost her husband and bread Mallikarjun Alias Mallikarjun Valikar vs The Head Master, New Age World School on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72631279/
3 earner of the family and children of the deceased were taken by her in-laws i.e., petitioner No.1 and 2.

sentences.text: Further submitted that, petitioner No.1 and 2 were residing with their elder sons i.e., Mohanand is X-Grampanchayat Chairman and 2nd son is Sadanand working in Dubai.

SCCH 5 Further submitted that, dependency is main criteria for claiming compensation, petitioner No.1 and 2 are not at all dependent on earnings of the deceased Rajkumar, hence petitioner No.1 and 2 are not entitled for compensation.
Accordingly prays to award compensation in her favour.
6. On going through the rival pleadings of the parties, my learned predecessor has framed the following:

::ISSUES::
1.

Whether the petitioners prove that, deceased Rajkumar @ Raja Kumara died in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 09.02.2023 at about 7.00 a.m. when deceased was riding Scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-50-EH- 7381 near 2nd Cross, Kodigehalli, Opposite to true Medical Health Partner, Thindlu Main Road,
Bengaluru at that time, School Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-50-B-2090 drivenby its driver in a rash and negligent manner dashed against the deceased and caused accident, as mentioned in claim petition?
SCCH 5 2.
Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?

3. What order or award?
7.

In order to prove their case, petitioner No.1 /father of the deceased has deposed his evidence as PW-1, further a Medical Record Technician at Victoria Hospital is examined as PW-2 and marked documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.21 and closed evidence.
Per contra, respondent No.3/ 2nd wife of the deceased is examined as RW-1 and marked documents as per Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.6 and closed evidence.
8. Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record.

Then my findings on the above issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:

9. Issue No.1:-

sentences.text: The petitioners inorder to prove their case, petitioner No.1/father of the deceased is examined as PW-1 and in his chief-examination evidence he has reiterated petition averments.

Though he has been elaborately cross-examined by the Respondent No.2 and 3 counsel, but nothing is brought on record to disbelieve the evidence of the PW-1.
10.

Apart from the oral evidence, the PW-1 has exhibited copy of FIR marked as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint is marked as Ex.P.2, copy of police intimation is marked as Ex.P.3, copy of death memo is marked as Ex.P.4, copy of requisition for addition of Sec.304(A) is marked as Ex.P.5, copy of spot mahazar with sketch is marked as Ex.P.6, copy of Sec.133 Notice with Reply is marked as Ex.P.7,
copy of AIR Reports are marked as Ex.P.8, copy of inquest is marked as Ex.P.9, copy of SCCH 5 P.M.Report is marked as Ex.P.10, copy of charge sheet is marked as Ex.P.11 which corroborates the case of the petitioners about causing of the death of Rajkumar out of the accident dated 09.02.2023 as alleged in the petition and in the evidence of PW-1.
11.
Further Medical Record Technician of Victoria Hospital is examined as PW-2.

Per contra,
respondent No.3/ 2nd wife of the deceased is examined as RW-1 and exhibited marriage memorandum marked as Ex.R.1, Notarized copy of marriage certificate marked as Ex.R.2, copy of Ration Card marked as Ex.R.3, copy Bank Pass Book marked as Ex.R.4, copy of Aadhar Card is marked as Ex.R.5 and copy of PAN Card is marked as Ex.R.6.
Except oral evidence of respondent No.3, respondents have not taken any endeavors to disprove the petitioner's case about non-causing of the accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.

Since in the absence of SCCH 5 iota of evidence, I have no hesitation to believe the case of the petitioners about death of deceased Raj Kumar out of the accident held on 09.02.2023 at about 7.00 a.m. when he was riding the scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-50-EH- 7381 on 2nd Cross, Kodigehalli, opp.
True Medical

Health Partner,
Thindlu Main Road, Bengaluru.
In the absence of iota of evidence, the arguments advanced by the petitioner's counsel are helpful to the case of the petitioner.
12. On the other hand, the police papers speaks that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of drivers of the school bus bearing Reg. No.KA-50-B-2090.

Under such circumstances, considering the said evidence and believing the evidence of the PW-1, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that,
petitioners have proved the above issue No.1 in their favour.
Accordingly I have answered above Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
SCCH 5 13. Issue No.2:-

As per the case of the petitioners, deceased/Raj Kumar was aged about 40 years as on the date of accident, for proof of age of the deceased, copy of aadhar card of the deceased marked as Ex.P.15, wherein date of birth of the deceased is mentioned as 10.06.1981, the alleged accident was occurred on 09.02.2023.

Accordingly relying on Ex.P.15, age of the deceased is considered about 42 years as on the date of accident, hence multiplier 14 is applicable with reference to decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Varma and Others V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and others.

sentences.text: As per the case of the petitioners, deceased was working as Helper & Delivery Man at Sri Laxmi Enterprises & Dunza, thereby earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.

In this regard, petitioners have exhibited copy of driving licence of the deceased marked as Ex.P.14, except this SCCH 5 they have not produced any documents to believe income of the deceased i.e., earnings Rs.30,000/-p.m.

Under such circumstances, with reference to the year of accident, relying upon the guidelines issued by Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru, notional income of the deceased is taken at the rate of Rs.15,250/- p.m. so that, said fact is taken into consideration for the purpose of calculation of loss of dependency.

sentences.text: 15. Further petitioner No.1 is father, petitioner No.2 is mother, petitioner No.3 and 4 are minor daughters of the deceased and respondent No.3 is 2 nd wife of the deceased/ Raj Kumar.
Inorder to prove their relationship with the deceased, petitioners have exhibited copy of aadhar cards marked as Ex.P.17, which reveals that, they are legal representatives of the deceased.

Further respondent No.3/2nd wife of the deceased has SCCH 5 exhibited marriage memorandum marked as Ex.R.1,
copy of marriage certificate marked as Ex.R.2, copy of ration card marked as Ex.R.3, copy of aadhar card marked as Ex.R.5, which discloses that, respondent No.3 is wife of the deceased Raj Kumar,
hence they will become dependents of the deceased.
16.

As per the case of Sarla Varma, if the number of dependents are 4 to 6, then 1/4th of the income is to be deducted towards personal and living expenses of the deceased, so that, 1/4th of the income will be deducted at the time of calculation of compensation amount.

17. In the Special Leave Petition (CIVIL) No.25590 of 2014 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd.,
V/s. Pranay Sethi, The Hon'ble Apex Court has made it clear that, an addition of 25% to be added to the monthly income, if the deceased was aged in between 40 to 50 years, in case of self employed person or person SCCH 5 having fixed salary as future prospects.

Further they are entitled for loss of estate of Rs.15,000/- and also they are entitled for funeral expenses for an amount of Rs.15,000/-.

20. During the course of arguments, petitioner counsel argued that, respondent No.3 is 2nd wife of the deceased, all petitioners are respondent No.3 are entitled for equal shares in compensation and respondent No.1 and respondent No.2 have not lead evidence etc.,
Accordingly said arguments are considered to an aforesaid extent.

21. Further inorder to prove their case, petitioners have examined Medical Record Technician at Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru as PW-2 and exhibited authorization SCCH 5 letter marked as Ex.P.19,
copy of MLC Extract marked as Ex.P.20 and case sheet marked as Ex.P.21.
In the cross- examination PW-2 has deposed that, he do not know the contents of the documents produced by him.

Further petitioners have produced medical prescriptions marked as Ex.P.12.
22.

1. Loss of dependency 24,01,896-00 2. Loss of consortium 20,000-00 (Respondent No.3)

4. Loss of parental consortium 40,000-00 (Rs.20,000/- each to Petitioner No.3 and 4)
5. Loss of Estate 15,000-00 6.
Funeral Expenses 15,000-00 Total 25,31,896-00 SCCH 5 23.

Accordingly I hold that, the Petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.25,31,896/-
with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.

24. In the case on hand, respondent No.2 being the insurer of the school bus bearing Reg.
No.KA-50-B-2090 has issued policy bearing No.993492223400000128 valid since 04.07.2022 to 03.07.2023, the alleged was occurred on 09.02.2023, which is valid as on the date of the accident.

Hence naturally liability of respondent No.1 shall go against respondent No.2, so that, respondent Mallikarjun Alias Mallikarjun Valikar vs The Head Master, New Age World School on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72631279/

SCCH 5 25. Issue No.3

: In view of the above reasoning and discussions to the above Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
::ORDER

: : 
The claim petition filed by the Petitioners under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioners and respondent No.3 are entitled for compensation of Rs.25,31,896/-
(Rupees Twenty Five Lakhs Thirty One Thousand Eight Hundred Ninety Six Only)
with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.2 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.
The Petitioners and respondent No.3 are entitled for compensation at the ratio 20:20:20:20:20 in the award amount.

The petitioners No.1, 2 and respondent No.3 are entitled to get release 60% of the award amount SCCH 5 through e-payment directly to their accounts on furnishing the Bank A/c details and remaining 40% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in their respective names.
Since Petitioner No.3 and 4 are minors, on deposit of the award amount, entire share shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank till he attains age of majority with a liberty to draw accrued interest in the name of minor Petitioner guardian on the said fixed deposit once in 3 months for the benefit of minor Petitioners.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the stenographer directly on the computer, typed by her, thereof is corrected and then pronounced by me in the Open Court on this the 7th day of February, 2025)
